title: [Perf] Add Triton config for DeepSeek V3 FP8 EP32 H200 (#23504)

image.wheel_note: first PyPI release after merge (2025-09-13 > 2025-08-24); picked by gen_tasks.py from PyPI upload dates.
image.build: docker build -t vllm-task:23504 -f tasks/pr_23504/workload/Dockerfile --build-arg VLLM_VERSION=0.10.2 --build-arg BASE_SHA=47455c424f62a20b75a7cfd872e17c5ba11c9f3a --build-arg MERGE_SHA=504d91431499e302bbd5a3d8a1432cd427ec8d5d tasks/pr_23504/workload

workload.note: W8A8 block FP8 Triton kernel tuning; GPU-only (H200 config).

policy.one_run_is: one `docker run` of the workload cmd per arm per repeat (same image, arm tree swapped in by the prelude)

contention_gate.rules: wait while another tenant uses the GPU (>5 % util or a foreign compute process >1 GiB) or the CPU (load1 > nproc/2)

arm_isolation.tree: wipe the wheel's vllm/*.py, copy the arm's vllm/ over site-packages (compiled .so stay)
arm_isolation.files: overlay ONLY metadata.json:source_files from the arm over the wheel's own tree
arm_isolation.tests_benchmarks: copied from the PR's merge tree to /t without a sibling vllm/ package

policy.noise_model: measure.py: paired log-speedup, MAD sigma, theta = clip(k*sigma, theta_min, theta_max) with k/theta from config.yaml:measure

headline: serving_throughput

reported.gain_evidence: The initial throughput number looked too good (1.6x speedup with tuning).

perf_gain.gain_evidence: The initial throughput number looked too good (1.6x speedup with tuning).

reported.experiments_note: reported = numbers from the PR body (author's machine)

hardware.gpu_hint: H200 (--tp-size 8 only shapes the problem; one GPU runs it)

standalone.run_baseline: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_23504:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=baseline vllm-task:23504 -lc 'A=/base; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_block_fp8.py --tp-size 8 --input-type fp8 --out-dtype float16 --block-n 128 --block-k 128'
standalone.run_pr_solution: docker run --rm --gpus device=0 --shm-size=2g -e CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID -e HF_HUB_DISABLE_PROGRESS_BARS=1 -v $PWD/tasks/pr_23504:/task:ro -v $PWD/.weights/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface -e ARM=pr_solution vllm-task:23504 -lc 'A=/gold; site=$(python3 -c "import vllm,os;print(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(vllm.__file__)))"); find "$site/vllm" -name "*.py" -delete; cp -a $A/vllm/. "$site/vllm/"; ln -sfn $A /src; rm -rf /t && mkdir -p /t && cd /gold && for d in tests benchmarks pyproject.toml conftest.py; do [ -e "$d" ] && cp -a "$d" /t/; done; cd /t; python3 benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_w8a8_block_fp8.py --tp-size 8 --input-type fp8 --out-dtype float16 --block-n 128 --block-k 128'
standalone.note: The image already holds both trees (/base = baseline commit, /gold = the PR's merge commit); the one-liner swaps the chosen tree over the installed wheel exactly like run_one.sh's prelude, then runs the workload cmd from /t (the merge tree's tests/ + benchmarks/).
